subject: TransitNexus - temporary processor announcement + evidence request
messages:
From: Thomas Keller <tkeller@transitnexus.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TransitNexus - temporary processor for log buffering (notice)

Hi Jasmine —

Quick heads up: TransitNexus will be acting as a transient processor for buffered ingestion on the FinAxis pilot. Scope is strictly buffering + short-term object staging (max 7 days) before pushing to FinAxis S3. No model data is stored; payloads are application logs and telemetry.

We onboarded last week and are providing the subprocessor declaration and a SOC 2 snapshot (attached). Key points:
- Data residency: Germany (eu-central-1) for temporary objects
- ACLs: objects encrypted at rest using TransitNexus-managed KMS keys; we can provide wrap/unwrapping proof
- Access: restricted to a small ops group with IP allowlist; no human access to decrypted payloads by default

Attaching: transitnexus-subproc-declaration-20260818.pdf and tnx-soc2-snapshot-202607.pdf

I understand FinAxis will want evidence and a short dataflow diagram — happy to join a call to walk through.

Best,
Thomas Keller
Head of Compliance | TransitNexus

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Keller <tkeller@transitnexus.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TransitNexus - temporary processor for log buffering (notice)

Thanks Thomas — and thanks for the attachments. Looping in Marissa (contracts) and Lauren (privacy) since FinAxis flagged this during procurement. Two quick asks to help accelerate approval: 

1) Can you confirm the exact KMS key ownership model and whether TransitNexus supports customer-managed key wrapping (we need to provide this option to customers in regulated EU deployments).
2) Will TransitNexus accept a narrow DPA addendum clause restricting the retention window to 7 days and forbidding downstream analytics on the buffered objects?

If you can reply inline we’ll forward to FinAxis with our recommended controls.

Jasmine
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Thomas Keller <tkeller@transitnexus.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TransitNexus - temporary processor for log buffering (notice)

Hi all — answering inline: 

> KMS key ownership model and CMK support?
We currently use customer-provided wrapping keys via AWS KMS External Key (Customer key material) for customers that request it. For the FinAxis pilot we can accept a customer-managed wrap key, though the unwrapping occurs in our ephemeral worker pool in eu-central-1. We will provide key ARNs and a short proof-of-invocation log sample.

> Narrow DPA addendum restricting retention to 7 days and forbidding downstream analytics?
Yes — TransitNexus is willing to sign a limited addendum. We need to triage the exact language with legal, but the ask is technically feasible and aligns with our retention controls.

I’ll attach a short dataflow diagram link here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1tNex-TransitNexus-DataflowDiagram

Thomas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: TransitNexus subprocessor notice + evidence — FinAxis follow-up

Sarah / FinAxis compliance team —

Forwarding TransitNexus’s notice and attachments. Short summary and next steps from Redwood: 
- TransitNexus will act solely as a transient buffer in eu-central-1, retention capped at 7 days.
- They confirmed support for customer-managed wrapping keys (CMK) and are open to a DPA addendum restricting analytics.

Requested from FinAxis: 
1) Confirmation that CMK + wrap-only invocation is acceptable. If so, we’ll request TransitNexus’s proof-of-invocation (sample logs).
2) Any additional controls required for your auditors (IP allowlist, personnel access audit).
3) If you want execution of a short addendum, we can route a DocuSign via our legal team (DocuSign link will be shared on approval).

Attachments referenced: transitnexus-subproc-declaration-20260818.pdf, tnx-soc2-snapshot-202607.pdf

—Marissa Cole
Sr. Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@finaxis.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Thomas Keller <tkeller@transitnexus.io>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TransitNexus subprocessor notice + evidence — FinAxis follow-up

Thanks Marissa — this looks reasonable. Quick answers from compliance: 
1) CMK wrap-only model is acceptable; we’ll want the proof-of-invocation sample and the KMS ARNs before go-live.
2) IP allowlist and a named personnel roster for ops access are required; please provide the last 90 days of access review logs if possible.
3) We do want the DPA addendum signed prior to the pilot; please send the DocuSign when ready.

If TransitNexus can provide the two short artifacts (KMS invocation sample + ops roster/access review), we can greenlight the pilot window next Monday.

Sarah Bennett
Head of Compliance | FinAxis
